tasks.spec:
Write a pytest file for the LLM response JSON extractor in the Fabrica 2 project.

IMPORTANT — where things live. Your current working directory is an isolated, TEMPORARY git worktree of the repository. It is deleted when your task passes. So you read source from inside it, but you write your deliverable to a durable absolute path outside it.

STEP 1 — Read the module you are testing, relative to your working directory:
  src/fabrica2/core/llm_response.py
Read it carefully before writing anything, including the private helper. Do not modify it or any other existing file. Do not run git commit; this worktree is temporary and any commit you make is discarded.

STEP 2 — Write exactly one new file, at this ABSOLUTE path:
  /tmp/ringer-fabrica2-tier/out/llm-response/test_llm_response.py
Create the directory if it does not exist. This is your deliverable and the only file you must produce.

WHAT THE MODULE DOES: extract_json(content, *, shortcut_keys=(), list_to_dict_key=None, log_label='LLM') pulls a structured value out of an LLM response. If content is a dict holding any of shortcut_keys at the top level, content is returned unchanged. Otherwise, if content['text'] is a string, four progressively more lenient parse strategies run in order: the whole text as JSON; a ```json fenced block; any ``` fenced block; then the substring from the first { to the last }. A raw top-level JSON list is rejected and yields None UNLESS list_to_dict_key is set, in which case it is normalised to {list_to_dict_key: [...]}. Anything that is not a dict falls through unchanged. Total parse failure logs a warning and returns None.

WHAT TO COVER — at least 12 test functions, including all of:
  1. Each of the four parse strategies succeeds on input that only that strategy can handle. Make the fenced-block cases genuinely mid-text, with prose before and after.
  2. shortcut_keys short-circuits: a dict containing one of the named keys is returned unchanged, and is the SAME object.
  3. shortcut_keys does NOT fire when none of the keys are present, so parsing proceeds.
  4. A raw top-level JSON list returns None when list_to_dict_key is unset, and is wrapped as {key: [...]} when it is set.
  5. Unparseable text returns None.
  6. Non-dict content (a string, a list, None) falls through and is returned unchanged.
  7. A dict whose 'text' is not a string falls through unchanged.
  8. The failure path logs a warning containing log_label. Use pytest's caplog fixture.

HOW TO WRITE IT:
  - Match the conventions of the existing tests in tests/unit/core/ inside your working directory. Read one first, for example tests/unit/core/test_check_result.py. Specifically: start with a module docstring, then `from __future__ import annotations`, and annotate every test function with `-> None`.
  - Keep every line at 100 characters or fewer, and use double quotes. The project lints with ruff.
  - Import extract_json from fabrica2.core.llm_response. Test the public function; do not test the private helper directly.
  - Every test must assert something real. Do not write a test whose body is only 'pass' or that asserts True.
  - Do not use network access. Do not install packages.

VERIFY BEFORE YOU FINISH: from your working directory, copy your deliverable into the tree and run it, exactly like this, until it passes:
  cp /tmp/ringer-fabrica2-tier/out/llm-response/test_llm_response.py tests/unit/core/
  PYTHONPATH="$PWD/src" /home/ph/epmc-tdm/fabrica2/.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/unit/core/test_llm_response.py -q --no-cov -p no:cacheprovider
When a test fails, decide whether your expectation or your test code is wrong, fix the file at the absolute path above, copy it in again and re-run. Never change the module under test to make a test pass. Make sure your final edits are saved to the absolute path, because that copy is what gets checked.

Collection output follows:"; printf '%s\n' "$COLLECT"; exit 1; fi; if ! PYTHONPATH="$PWD/src" $PY -m pytest "$F" -q --no-cov -p no:cacheprovider; then echo "FAIL: pytest reported failing tests in the deliverable (full pytest output is above)."; exit 1; fi; if ! grep -q 'list_to_dict_key' "$OUT"; then echo "FAIL: the deliverable never exercises list_to_dict_key, so the list-normalisation branch is untested."; exit 1; fi; if ! grep -q 'caplog' "$OUT"; then echo "FAIL: the deliverable never uses caplog, so the warning-on-failure path is untested."; exit 1; fi; echo "OK: $N tests collected and passed against the worktree's own source; deliverable is safe at $OUT"
tasks.verified: The deliverable holds at least 12 tests that all pass against the worktree's own copy of llm_response, exercising all four parse strategies plus the list-normalisation and warning-logging branches.

Write a pytest file for the analyzer descriptor model in the Fabrica 2 project.

IMPORTANT — where things live. Your current working directory is an isolated, TEMPORARY git worktree of the repository. It is deleted when your task passes. So you read source from inside it, but you write your deliverable to a durable absolute path outside it.

STEP 1 — Read the module you are testing, relative to your working directory:
  src/fabrica2/core/analyzer_descriptor.py
It imports enums from other modules (SourceAccessMode, DisclosureLevel, and profile types). Read those too, enough to construct valid values. Do not modify any existing file. Do not run git commit; this worktree is temporary and any commit you make is discarded.

STEP 2 — Write exactly one new file, at this ABSOLUTE path:
  /tmp/ringer-fabrica2-tier/out/analyzer-descriptor/test_analyzer_descriptor.py
Create the directory if it does not exist. This is your deliverable and the only file you must produce.

WHAT THE MODULE DEFINES: AnalyzerEngine, a StrEnum with exactly the members CODE ('code'), AI_ML ('ai_ml') and LLM ('llm'); and AnalyzerDescriptor, a pydantic model. Its fields include name, title and description (strings), engine (defaulting to AnalyzerEngine.CODE), several frozenset fields with default factories (supported_types, disclosure_levels, requires_access_modes), generator_hint (defaulting to an empty string), the booleans planner_relevant and value_revealing (both defaulting to False), and sample_finding, which is an optional AnalyzerFinding defaulting to None.

WHAT TO COVER — at least 12 test functions, including all of:
  1. A minimal valid AnalyzerDescriptor constructs, and EVERY documented default holds — check each one explicitly rather than in a single assertion.
  2. AnalyzerEngine is a StrEnum, so each member equals its own string value.
  3. Every AnalyzerEngine member is accepted as an engine value. Iterate the enum rather than hard-coding the members, so the test keeps working when the enum grows.
  4. An engine value outside the enum raises pydantic.ValidationError.
  5. The frozenset fields are genuinely frozensets after construction, and a list or set passed in is coerced to one.
  6. Passing a duplicate-containing sequence to a frozenset field de-duplicates it.
  7. sample_finding accepts None and accepts a valid AnalyzerFinding.
  8. A missing required field raises ValidationError.
  9. A fully populated descriptor round-trips through model_dump() and back through the constructor to an equal object.

HOW TO WRITE IT:
  - Match the conventions of the existing tests in tests/unit/core/ inside your working directory. Read one first, for example tests/unit/core/test_check_result.py. Specifically: start with a module docstring, then `from __future__ import annotations`, and annotate every test function with `-> None`.
  - Keep every line at 100 characters or fewer, and use double quotes. The project lints with ruff.
  - Import from fabrica2.core.analyzer_descriptor, and import any enum you need from the module that actually defines it.
  - Every test must assert something real. Do not write a test whose body is only 'pass' or that asserts True.
  - Do not use network access. Do not install packages.

When a test fails, decide whether your expectation or your test code is wrong, fix the file at the absolute path above, copy it in again and re-run. Never change the module under test to make a test pass. Make sure your final edits are saved to the absolute path, because that copy is what gets checked.

Write a pytest file for the tilt audit model in the Fabrica 2 project.

IMPORTANT — where things live. Your current working directory is an isolated, TEMPORARY git worktree of the repository. It is deleted when your task passes. So you read source from inside it, but you write your deliverable to a durable absolute path outside it.

STEP 1 — Read the module you are testing, relative to your working directory:
  src/fabrica2/core/tilt_audit.py
Read it carefully before writing anything, including its model_config. Do not modify it or any other existing file. Do not run git commit; this worktree is temporary and any commit you make is discarded.

STEP 2 — Write exactly one new file, at this ABSOLUTE path:
  /tmp/ringer-fabrica2-tier/out/tilt-audit/test_tilt_audit.py
Create the directory if it does not exist. This is your deliverable and the only file you must produce.

WHAT THE MODULE DEFINES: TiltAuditEntry, a pydantic model. Note its model_config carefully — it sets extra='allow' and frozen=True. That means undeclared keyword arguments are ACCEPTED and kept, which is the opposite of most models in this codebase; do not assume extras are forbidden. Fields include tilt_source (a string of 1 to 200 characters), tilt_kind (a string), tilt_intent (free-form, defaulting to None), tilt_intent_mode (optional string defaulting to None), realized (free-form, defaulting to None), divergence (a bool defaulting to False) and extra_context (a dict defaulting to empty).

WHAT TO COVER — at least 12 test functions, including all of:
  1. A minimal valid TiltAuditEntry constructs, and EVERY documented default holds — check each one explicitly rather than in a single assertion.
  2. extra='allow' works: an undeclared keyword argument is accepted AND is readable back off the constructed object. Assert the value survives, not merely that construction did not raise.
  3. frozen=True works: assigning to a field after construction raises. Catch it with pytest.raises((TypeError, ValueError)) so the test does not depend on pydantic's exact exception type.
  4. tilt_source rejects the empty string and rejects a string longer than its maximum. Derive the boundary from the limit stated in the module rather than guessing, and also assert that a string at exactly the limit is accepted.
  5. The free-form fields (tilt_intent, realized) accept several different types — at least a string, a number, a list and a dict.
  6. extra_context accepts a populated dict and preserves it exactly.
  7. divergence accepts both True and False.
  8. A missing required field raises pydantic.ValidationError.
  9. A fully populated entry, including an extra undeclared field, round-trips through model_dump() and back through the constructor to an equal object.

HOW TO WRITE IT:
  - Match the conventions of the existing tests in tests/unit/core/ inside your working directory. Read one first, for example tests/unit/core/test_check_result.py. Specifically: start with a module docstring, then `from __future__ import annotations`, and annotate every test function with `-> None`.
  - Keep every line at 100 characters or fewer, and use double quotes. The project lints with ruff.
  - Import from fabrica2.core.tilt_audit, and import ValidationError from pydantic.
  - Every test must assert something real. Do not write a test whose body is only 'pass' or that asserts True.
  - Do not use network access. Do not install packages.

When a test fails, decide whether your expectation or your test code is wrong, fix the file at the absolute path above, copy it in again and re-run. Never change the module under test to make a test pass. Make sure your final edits are saved to the absolute path, because that copy is what gets checked.
